title: Microsoft Purview: allow version trimming for content under retention in SharePoint and OneDrive
summary: Hold: the retention-policy licensing paragraph omits the different licence requirements for adaptive policy scopes, which could mislead administrators budgeting with E3 or Business Premium. The roadmap facts and published version-management commands are supported; documentation for the planned retention override remains unpublished.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a Purview Data Lifecycle Management setting allowing version trimming on SharePoint and OneDrive content covered by retention policies.
claims.quote: Admins with appropriate Purview RBAC can enable version cleanup for ODB/SPO content even when retention policies are in effect.

claims.claim: The planned setting is policy-scoped and overrides the default retention of all versions.
claims.quote: This would be a policy scoped setting that essentially overrides the default behavior where all versions are retained.

claims.claim: The planned trimming excludes specific protected cases.
claims.quote: When turned on, SharePoint’s version management will be permitted to trim file versions per the defined limits except for specific protected cases.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAutoExpirationVersionTrim $true sets automatic organization version limits for new libraries.
claims.quote:
To set Automatic version history limits for all new document libraries created in your organization using PowerShell, run the following command:
Set-SPOTenant -EnableAutoExpirationVersionTrim $true

claims.claim: Changes to organization-level default limits apply to new SharePoint libraries and new OneDrive accounts rather than updating existing libraries.
claims.quote: Changes made to organization-level version history limits apply to new SharePoint libraries and OneDrive user accounts created since the change was made.

claims.claim: Changing organization-level version defaults does not trim existing versions.
claims.quote: Changes made to the organization-level version history limits will not trim existing version history to the new limits.

claims.claim: Manual organization version limits use Set-SPOTenant's -MajorVersionLimit parameter.
claims.quote:
Set-SPOTenant `
    -EnableAutoExpirationVersionTrim $false `
    -MajorVersionLimit <int> `
    -ExpireVersionsAfterDays <int, 0 for no expiration>

claims.claim: Manual organization version limits use Set-SPOTenant's -ExpireVersionsAfterDays parameter.
